*tūḍ*—some say so. 352 *huḍḍha*, 353 *hūḍḍa* (4)—these are from the Dhātupāṭha. 354 *hoḍ* in the sense of going; 355 *rauḍha* in the sense of disrespect; 356 *roḍa*, 357 *loḍḍha* in the sense of madness; 358 *aḍa* in the sense of exertion; 359 *laḍa* in the sense of sport. Some say *lala*. 360 *kaḍha* in the sense of intoxication. Some say *kāḍa*. 361 *gahi* in the sense of a part of the face. The roots beginning with *śauṭra* are udātta, have an udātta indicatory letter (*it*), and are parasmaipada. 362 *tiṭa*, 363 *teṣu*, 364 *ṣṭiṭa*, 365 *ṣṭeṭa*—these have the meaning of trickling. *Teṭa* also has the meaning of trembling.

366 *gleṣ* in dejection; 367 *ṭutreṭa* in trembling; 368 *kepṛ*, 369 *pa*, 370 *glaṃ* [in the sense of going]; 372 *meṭa*, 372 *repṛ*, 373 *leṭa* in going; 374 *trapūṣ* in shame; 375 *kapi* in moving; 376 *ravi*, 377 *lavi*, 378 *avi* in sound; 379 *chavi* in falling away and [sound]; 380 *kavṛ* in color; 381 *kī* and 382 *kṣīvṛ* in intoxication; 383 *śībhṛ* in boasting; 384 *cibhṛ* also [in boasting]; 385 *rebhṛ* in sound. *Abhi* and *rabhi* are sometimes mentioned [as prefixes].

386. *ṣṭabhi* (387. *skabhi*) in the sense of obstructing; 388. *nabhi* (389. *jubhi*) in the sense of bending a limb; 390. *śalbha* in the sense of boasting; 391. *valbha* in the sense of eating; 392. *galbha* in the sense of audacity; 393. *śrambhu* in the sense of negligence. It also begins with a dental [d]. 394. *ṣṭubhu* in the sense of supporting. The roots beginning with *tipi* are udātta, anudāttet, and ātmanepadī; however, *tipi* itself is anudātta. 395. *gup* in the sense of protecting; 396. *dhūpa* in the sense of heating; 397. *japa* (398. *jalpa*) in the sense of distinct speech. 399. ...

400. *japa* (to mutter) is used in the sense of mental recitation (*mānasa*). 401. *capa* (to soothe). 402. *papa* (to assemble). 403. *rapa*, 404. *lapa* (to speak articulately). 405. *cupa* (to move slowly). 406. *tupa*, 407. *tumpa*, 408. *trupa*, 409. *numpa*, 410. *tupha*, 411. *tumpha*, 412. *trupha*, 413. *trumpha*—these have the meaning of injury (*hiṃsā*).

413 *parṣa*, 414 *rapha*, 415 *raphi*, 416 *arba*, 417 *parva*, 418 *larva*, 419 *varṣa*, 420 *marca*, 421 *karva*, 422 *kharva*, 423 *garva*, 424 *śarva*, 425 *parva*, 426 *carva*—these mean "to go. 467 *kubi* means "to cover. 428 *lubi*, 429 *tubi* mean "to crush. 430 *cuvi* means "to bring the mouth together [in kissing]. 431 *pṛbhu*, 432 *pṛmbhu* mean "to injure. Some say *pibhu* and *ṣimbhu*. 433 *śubha*, 434 *śumbha* mean "to speak. Some say "to shine. Others say "to injure."

The roots beginning with *gup* are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), take the *udātta-ita* designation, and are *parasmaipada*. 435 *ghiṇi*, 436 *ghuṇi*, 437 *ghṛṇi*—in the sense of grasping; 438 *ghuṇa*, 439 *ghūrṇa*—in the sense of wandering; 440 *paṇa*—in the sense of trade and praise; 441 *pana*—also [in the same senses]; 442 *bhāma*—in the sense of anger; 443 *kṣamūp*—in the sense of enduring; 444 *kamu*—in the sense of desire. The roots beginning with *ghiṇi* are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), have the *anudātta-ita* designation, and are *ātmanepada*.

445. *aṇ*, 446. *raṇ*, 447. *vaṇ*, 448. *bhaṇ*, 449. *maṇ*, 450. *kaṇ*, 451. *kaṇ*, 452. *vraṇ*, 453. *bhraṇ*, 454. *dhvaṇ*—these have the meaning of "sound. Some also include *dhaṇ*. 455. *oṭa* in the sense of "removing. 456. *śauṇa* in the senses of "color" and "motion. 457. *śroṇa* in the sense of "collection. 458. *śloṇa* also [in the same sense]. 459. *paiṇa* in the senses of "going," "death," and "joining. 460. *dhaṇ* in the sense of "sound. Some also include *raṇ*. 461. *kanī* in the senses of "light," "beauty," and "motion. 462. *ṭana*, 463. *vana* in the sense of "sound."

464. *vana* and 465. *ṣaṇa* in the sense of sharing or serving. 466. *ama* in the sense of going and so forth. 467. *drama*, 468. *hamma*, and 469. *mīma* in the sense of going. 470. *camu*, 471. *chamu*, 472. *jamu*, and 473. *jhamu* in the sense of eating. 474. *kamu* in the sense of stepping with the feet. The roots beginning with *aṇ* (464) are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), have an acute accent on the radical vowel (*udāttet*), and are conjugated in the Parasmaipada. 475. *aya*, 476. *vaya*, 477. *paya*, 478. *maya*, 479. *naya*, 480. *taya*, and 481. *ṇaya* in the sense of going. 482. *daya* in the senses of giving, going, protecting, harming, and taking. 483. *raya* in the sense of going. This concludes the *Bhvādi* group.

485. *Ūyī* in the sense of weaving or extending a thread. 486. *Pūyī* in the sense of dissolution and foul odor. 487. *Krūthī* in the sense of sound and wetting. 488. *Kṣmāyī* in the sense of shaking. 489. *Sphāyī* and 490. *Opyāyī* in the sense of growth. 491. *Tāyṛ* in the sense of continuity and protection. 492. *Śala* in the sense of moving and covering. 493. *Vala* and 494. *Valla* in the sense of covering and moving about. 495. *Mala* and 496. *Malla* in the sense of holding. 497. *Bhala* and 498. *Bhalla* in the sense of reproaching, injury, and giving. 499. *Kala* in the sense of sound and counting.

499. *kalla* in the sense of an indistinct sound; Svāmī says "in the sense of not being a sound. 500. *tevṛ* 501. *devṛ* in the sense of playing. 502. *ṣevṛ* 503. *gevṛ* 504. *glevṛ* 505. *pevṛ* 506. *mevṛ* 507. *mlevṛ* in the sense of serving. Some say *śevṛ*, *khevṛ*, and *klevṛ*. 508. *revṛ* in the sense of leaping and moving. The roots beginning with *ay* (i.e., from *ay* onwards) are udātta, have anudātta indicatory letters (*it*), and are conjugated in the Ātmanepada. 509. *mavya* in the sense of binding. 510. *sūrya* 511. *īrdhya* 512. *īrṣya*—these have the meaning of envy. 513. *haya* in the sense of going. 514. *śucya* in the sense of pressing.

*cuca*—some say [this root exists]. 515 *harya* in the sense of motion and desire. 516 *ala* in the senses of ornamenting, sufficiency, and warding off. Some say this [root] has a svarita accent. 517 *ñi phalā* in the sense of falling apart. 518 *mīla*, 519 *mīla*, 520 *smīla*, 521 *kṣmīla* in the sense of closing the eyes. 522 *pīla* in the sense of obstructing. 523 *nīla* in the sense of color. 524 *śīla* in the sense of concentration. 525 *kīla* in the sense of binding. 526 *kūla* in the sense of covering. 527 *śūla* in the sense of pain and also in the sense of a loud sound. 528 *tūla* in the sense of extracting. 529 *pūla* in the sense of a cluster.

530 *mūla* [is used] in the sense of establishing; 531 *phala* in the sense of production; 532 *culla* in the sense of making small; 533 *phulla* in the sense of blossoming; 534 *cilla* in the sense of slackness and making small; 535 *tila* in the sense of motion. Some say *tilla*. 536 *veḷ*, 537 *cela*, 538 *kela*, 539 *khela*, 540 *kṣvela*, 541 *vella* in the sense of moving; 542 *pela*, 543 *phela*, 544 *śela* in the sense of going. Some say *ṣela*. 545 *skhala* in the sense of stumbling; 546 *khala* in the sense of accumulation; 547 *gala* in the sense of eating.

548. *ṣala* in the sense of going; 549. *dala* in the sense of splitting; 550. *śvala*, 551. *valla* in the sense of swift motion; 552. *khola*, 553. *khorṛ* in the sense of obstructing movement; 554. *dhorṛ* in the sense of skill in movement; 555. *tsara* in the sense of moving by stealth; 556. *kmara* in the sense of reeling; 557. *abhra*, 558. *vabhra*, 559. *mabhra*, 560. *cara*—these have the meaning of "going. *Carati* is also used in the sense of eating. 561. *ṣṭhivu* in the sense of spitting out; 562. *ji* in the sense of victory; 563. *jīva* in the sense of sustaining life.

564 *pīva*, 565 *mība*, 566 *tīva*, 567 *ṇīva*—[these] mean stoutness. 568 *kṣivu*, 569 *kṣeṣu*—[these] mean casting out. 570 *uva*, 571 *turvī*, 572 *thurvī*, 573 *duva*, 574 *dhurvī*—[these] have the sense of harming. 575 *gurvī*—[this means] lifting up. 576 *murvī*—[this means] binding. 577 *purva*, 580 *carva*, 581 *bharva*—[these] mean filling. 582 *karva*, 583 *kharva*, 584 *garva*—[these] mean pride. 585 *arba*, 586 *śarva*, 587 *ṣarva*—[these] mean harming.

588. *ivi* in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*). 589. *pibi*, 590. *mivi*, 591. *ṇivi* in the sense of sprinkling (*secana*); some say in the sense of serving (*sevane*). 592. *hivi*, 593. *divi*, 594. *ghivi*, 595. *jivi* have the meaning of pleasing (*mīṇana*). 596. *rivi*, 597. *ravi*, 598. *dhavi* have the meaning of motion (*gati*). 599. *kṛvi* in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*) and doing (*karaṇa*). 600. *mava* in the sense of binding (*bandhana*).

601. The roots beginning with *ava*—meaning protection, motion, splendor, affection, satisfaction, understanding, entry, hearing, lordship, begging, action, desire, radiance, attainment, embracing, injury, giving, a share, and increase—are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*) and take the *parasmaipada* endings; however, *ji* is unaccented (*anudātta*). 602. *dhāvu* means motion and purification; it is accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), belongs to the *svādi* class, and is used in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣa*). 603. *dhukṣa*; 604. *dhikṣa* mean to kindle. [The following is from] the Dhātupāṭha: [the root *nakṣ*] means to perish, to suffer, and to live. 605. *vṛkṣa* means to cover or obstruct.

606. *Śikṣ* in the sense of acquiring knowledge. 607. *Bhikṣ* in the sense of begging, whether there be no gain or gain. 608. *Kleś* in the sense of indistinct speech; Durga says it means "to afflict. 609. *Dakṣ* in the sense of growth and quickness. 610. *Dīkṣ* in the sense of shaving the head, sacrifice, initiation (*upanayana*), and the instruction of rules and vows. 611. *Īkṣ* in the sense of seeing. 612. *Īṣ* in the sense of motion, injury, and seeing. 613. *Bhāṣ* in the sense of distinct speech. 614. *Varṣ* in the sense of moistening. 615. *Geṣṭ* in the sense of seeking; some say *gleṣ*.

616. *peṭ* in the sense of effort; 617. *jeṭ*; 618. *ṇeṣu*; 619. *eṭa*; 620. *meṣṭha* in the sense of motion; 621. *reṣu*; 622. *dveṣu*; 623. *he* in the sense of indistinct sound; 624. *kāsṛ* in the sense of contemptuous sound; 625. *bhāsa* in the sense of shining; 626. *ṇāsa*; 627. *rāsa* in the sense of sound; 628. *ṇasa* in the sense of crookedness; 629. *bhyasa* in the sense of fear; 630. *āṅ-śasi* in the sense of desire; 631. *grasu*; 632. *glasu* in the sense of eating; 633. *īha* in the sense of exertion; 634. *vahi*; 635. *mahi* in the sense of growth; 636. *ahi* in the sense of motion.

637. *garha* and 638. *galha* are used in the sense of censuring (*kutsā*). 639. *varha* and 640. *balha* are used in the sense of preeminence (*prādhānya*). 641. *varha* and 642. *valha* are used in the senses of reviling (*paribhāṣaṇa*), injuring (*hiṃsā*), and covering (*cchādana*). 643. *plih* is used in the sense of going (*gati*). 644. *vehra*, 645. *jeha*, and 646. *bāhra* are used in the sense of effort (*prayatna*). *Jeha* is also used in the sense of going (*gati*). 647. *dāha* is used in the sense of the cessation of sleep (*nidrākṣaya*). According to some, it means depositing (*nikṣepa*). 648. *kāḍhā* is used in the sense of shining (*dīpti*). 649. *ūha* is used in the sense of deliberation (*vitarke*). 650. *gāhū* is used in the sense of stirring or agitating (*viloḍana*). 651. *gṛhū* is used in the sense of censuring (*garhaṇa*). 652. *glaha* is also [used in that sense]. 653. *ghuṣi* is used in the sense of making beautiful or manifesting splendor (*kāntikaraṇa*).

Some say [the root] *ghuṣ* [is included]. The roots beginning with *dhukṣ* are udātta, anudāttet, and ātmanepada. 654. *ghuṣir* in the sense of making a sound (not "noise"). 655. *akṣū* in the sense of pervading. 656. *takṣū* and 657. *tvakṣū* in the sense of making thin. 658. *ukṣa* in the sense of sprinkling. 659. *rakṣa* in the sense of protecting. 660. *ṇikṣa* in the sense of kissing. 661. *tṛkṣa*, 662. *ṣṭṛkṣa*, and 663. *ṇakṣa* in the sense of going. 664. *vakṣa* in the sense of anger; some say in the sense of gathering (*saṃghāta*). 665. *mṛkṣa* in the sense of gathering; some say *vrakṣa*. 666. *takṣa* in the sense of skinning.

667. *sūrks* (to pay heed, to be careful). 668. *kākṣi*, 669. *vākṣi*, 670. *mākṣi* (in the sense of longing). 671. *dākṣi*, 672. *ghrākṣi*, 673. *dhvākṣi* (and in the sense of a fierce howling). 674. *cūṣa* (in drinking). 675. *tūṣa* (in contentment). 676. *pūṣa* (in growth). 677. *mūṣa* (in stealing). 678. *lūṣa*, 679. *rūṣa* (in adorning). 680. *śūṣa* (in procreation). 681. *yūṣa* (in injury). 682. *jūṣa* (also [in this sense]). 683. *bhūṣa* (in ornamenting). 684. *ūṣa* (in pain). 685. *īṣa* (in rising up).

686 *kapa*, 687 *khaṣa*, 688 *śiṣa*, 689 *japa*, 690 *jhaṣa*, 691 *śaṣa*, 692 *varṣa*, 693 *maṣa*, 694 *ruṣa*, 695 *riṣa*—these have the meaning of "injury" (*hiṃsā*). 696 *bhaṣa* means "threatening" (*bhartsana*). 697 *uṣa* means "burning" (*dāha*). 698 *jiṣu*, 699 *viṣu*, 700 *miṣu*—these mean "moistening" (*secana*). 701 *puṣa* means "nourishing" (*puṣṭi*). 702 *śriṣu*, 703 *śliṣu*, 704 *pruṣu*, 705 *ṛṣu*—these mean "burning. 706 *pṛṣu*, 707 *vṛṣu*, 708 *mṛṣu*—these mean "moistening"; *mṛṣu* also means "enduring" (*sahana*), while the other two [mean] "injury" and "crushing" (*hiṃsā-saṃkleśana*). 709 *ghṛṣu* means "rubbing together" (*saṃgharṣa*).

710 *hṛṣu* in the sense of falsehood; 711 *tusa*, 712 *hūsa*, 713 *lasa*, 714 *rasa* in the sense of sound; 715 *lasa* in the sense of clinging and playing; 716 *ghasla* in the sense of eating; 717 *jarja*, 718 *carca*, 719 *jharjha* in the senses of reproaching, injuring, and threatening; 720 *pisṛ*, 721 *pesṛ* in the sense of going; 722 *hasa* in the sense of laughing; 723 *ṇiśa* in the sense of concentration; 724 *miśa*, 725 *maśa* in the senses of sound and causing anger; 726 *śava* in the sense of going; 727 *śaśa* in the sense of moving swiftly; 728 *śasu* in the sense of injuring; 729 *śaṃsu* in the sense of praising.

Some say [the root *duh*] means "in a miserable state. 730 *cah* in the sense of "calculation"; 731 *maha* in the sense of "worship"; 732 *raha* in the sense of "abandoning"; 733 *rahi* in the sense of "going. 734 *dṛha*, 735 *dṛhi*: these belong to the *bhvādi* class. (7) 736 *vṛha*, 737 *bṛhi* in the sense of "growing. Some say that *vṛhi* also means "sound" and that there is a root *bṛhi*. 738 *tuhi*, 739 *buhi*, 740 *uhi* in the sense of "breaking. 741 *arha* in the sense of "worship. The roots beginning with *ghuṣi* have an acute accent on the first syllable (*udātta*) and are marked with an indicatory letter *it* (*udāttet*), and they take the *parasmaipada* endings. However, *ghas* is unaccented (*anudātta*). 742 *dyuta* in the sense of "shining"; 743 *śvitā* in the sense of "color."

744. *trimidā* (trimidā) in the sense of moistening (*snehana*). 745. *ñiṣvidā* (ñiṣvidā) in the senses of moistening (*snehana*) and releasing (*mocana*); some say it means delusion (*mohana*); others say there is also *ñividā*. 746. *ruca* (ruca) in the senses of shining (*dīpti*) and desire (*abhilāṣa*). 747. *ghuṭa* (ghuṭa) in the sense of turning over (*parivartana*). 748. *ruṭa*, 749. *luṭa*, 750. *luṭha* in the sense of striking against (*pratighāta*). 751. *śubha* (śubha) in the sense of shining. 752. *kṣubha* (kṣubha) in the sense of agitation (*saṃcalana*). 753. *ṇabha* (ṇabha), 754. *tubha* in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*); the first also [means] non-existence (*abhāva*). 755. *sraṃsu*, 756. *vaṃsu*, 757. *bhraṃsu* in the sense of falling down (*avasraṃsana*). 758. *dhvaṃsu* also in the sense of going (*gati*).

Some also include *bhrūśū*. 758 *sambhu* in the sense of trust; 759 *vṛtu* in the sense of turning; 760 *vṛdhu* in the sense of growth; 761 *śṛdhu* in the sense of contemptuous sound; 762 *syandū* in the sense of flowing; 763 *kṛpū* in the sense of capability. The roots beginning with *dyut* are udātta, anudāttet, and ātmanepadī. [End of] *vṛt*. 764 *ghaṭa* in the sense of exertion; 765 *vyatha* in the sense of fear and trembling; 766 *patha* in the sense of making known; 767 *masa* in the sense of expansion; 768 *sada* in the sense of crushing; 769 *skhada* in the sense of moving about.

770. *kṣaji* (meaning "to go" and "to give"). 771. *dakṣi* (meaning "to be able"). 772. *kṛpa* (in the sense of compassion and "to go"). 773. *kadi*, 774. *ṛdi*, 775. *kkadi* (in the sense of "distress"; some say "deficiency"). Nandin says all three are *anidita* (not having the *it*-augment); Svāmin says they are *idita* (having the *it*-augment). Maitreya says *kavi* and *kadi* are *idita*, while *kada* and *kkada* are *anidita*. 776. *ñitvarā* (in the sense of "agitation"). The roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are marked with *ṣ*. They are udātta, have the anudātta accent on the root vowel, and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voice). 777. *jvara* (in the sense of "disease"). 778. *gaḍa* (in the sense of "to sprinkle").

779. *heḍ* in the sense of surrounding; 780. *vaṭa*, 781. *bhaṭa* in the sense of censuring; 782. *ṇaṭ* in the sense of dancing (others say "in the sense of going"); 783. *ṭaka* in the sense of striking back; 784. *caka* in the sense of satiety; 785. *kakhe* in the sense of laughing; 786. *rage* in the sense of apprehension; 787. *lage* in the sense of attachment; 788. *nhage*, 789. *hage*, 790. *ṣage*, 791. *ṭage* in the sense of covering; 792. *ko* is not [included] in the list (*nocyate*); 793. *aka*, 794. *aga* in the sense of crooked motion; 795. *kaṇa*, 796. *raṇa* in the sense of going; 797. *caṇa*, 798. *śaṇa*, 799. *śraṇa* in the sense of giving as well.

Others say that *śaṇ* means "to go. Now: 801 *ślatha*, 802 *ṛtha*, 803 *klatha*—these have the sense of "injury. 804 *cana* and 805 *vana* are not mentioned [as separate roots]. 806 *nvala* means "to shine. 807 *hvala* and 808 *hāla* mean "to move. 809 *smṛ* means "to reflect" (*ādhyāna*). 810 *dṛ* means "fear. 811 *nṛ* means "to lead. 812 *śrā* means "cooking. 813 *jñā* [is used] in the senses of killing, pleasing, and calming. 814 *cali* means "trembling. 815 *chadir* means "strengthening. 816 *laḍi* means "licking" or "agitating the tongue. 817 *madī* means "joy" and "intoxication."

818. *dhvan* in the sense of sound; 819. *dal*, 820. *val*, 821. *skhal*, 822. *raṇ*, 823. *dhvan*, 824. *trap*, 825. *kṣapay*—thus says Bhoja; 826. *svan* in the sense of adorning. The roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are *mit*. 827. *jan*, 828. *jūṣ*, 829. *kras*, 830. *rañj*, and those ending in *-am*; 832. *jval*, 833. *hmal*, 834. *nam*—these optionally [take *niṣṭhā*] when without a prefix; 836. *glā*, 837. *snā*, 838. *van*, 839. *vṛm*—and these do not [take *niṣṭhā*]; 840. *kam*, 841. *am*, 842. *cam*; 843. *śam* in the sense of seeing.

844. *yama* (to restrain), with the exception of *pari-veṣaṇa*. 845. *skhadira*, also after *ava* and *pari*. 846. *phaṇa* (to move). The roots beginning with *ghaṭ* and ending with *phaṇa* are marked as *mit*. [This concludes] the section on *vṛt*. The roots beginning with *jvara* are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), have an indicatory vowel *it* (*udāttet*), and are conjugated in the Parasmaipada. 847. *rājū* (to shine); it is accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), has an indicatory letter *k* (*svarita*), and is conjugated in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣa*). 848. *dhu* (the root *dhātupāṭha*). 849. *ṭubhrāgṛ*. 850. *ṭubhchāgṛ*; [all] these mean "to shine. These are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), have an indicatory vowel *ṅ* (*anudāttet*), and are conjugated in the Ātmanepada. 851. *syamu*. 852. *svana*. 853. *dhvana*; [all] these mean "sound."

854 *ṣama* 855 *ṣṭama*, in the sense of non-deficiency (*avaikalye*). [Roots ending in] *vṛt*. 856 *jvala*, in the sense of flaming (*dīptau*). 857 *cala*, in the sense of trembling (*kampane*). 858 *jala*, in the sense of striking (*ghātane*). 859 *ṭala* 860 *ṭūvala*, in the sense of deficiency (*vaikalye*). 861 *sthala*, in the sense of standing/firmness (*sthāne*). 862 *hala*, in the sense of plowing/scraping (*vilekhane*). 863 *gala*, in the sense of odor (*gandhe*). Some say "in the sense of binding" (*bandhane*). 864 *pala*, in the sense of going (*gatau*). 865 *vala*, in the sense of living (*prāṇane*) and enclosing grain (*dhānyāvarodhane*). 866 *pula*, in the sense of greatness (*mahattve*). 867 *kula*, in the sense of gathering (*saṃstyāne*) and among kinsmen (*bandhuṣu*).

868 *śala*, 869 *hula*, 870 *patla*—in the sense of going. 871 *katha*—in the sense of cooking. 872 *patha*—in the sense of going. 873 *matha*—in the sense of churning. 874 *ṭuvama*—in the sense of vomiting. 875 *bhramu*—in the sense of wandering. 876 *kṣara*—in the sense of moving. The roots beginning with *syām* are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), have an indicatory vowel *ṅ* (*udāttet*), and are conjugated in the Parasmaipada. 877 *ṣaha*—in the sense of enduring. This root is accented on the first syllable (*udātta*), has an indicatory vowel *ṇ* (*anudātta*), and is conjugated in the Ātmanepada. 878 *ramu*—in the sense of sporting. 880. *śadūl* (śātane) – to destroy. 881. *kruś* (āhvāne rodane ca) – to call out and to weep. The three roots beginning with *sad* (878–880) are anudātta, have an udātta indicatory letter (*it*), and are parasmaipada. 882. *kuc* (saṃparcanakauṭilyapratiṣṭambhavilekhaneṣu) – to mix, to be crooked, to obstruct, and to scratch. 883. *budh* (avagamane) – to understand. 884. *ruh* (bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca) – to grow from a seed and to appear. 885. *kas* (gatau) – to move. [End of section] *vṛt*. The roots beginning with *kuc* (882–885) are udātta, have an udātta indicatory letter, and are parasmaipada; however, *ruh* is anudātta. 886. *hikka* (avyakte śabde) – to make an indistinct sound.

887. *Añcu* means "to go" and "to beg. Some say the root is *acu*; others say it is *aci*. 888. *Ṭuyācū* means "to beg. 889. *Reṭṭa* means "to speak abusively. 890. *Cate* and 891. *cade* mean "to beg. 892. *Moṭa* means "to be sufficient. 893. *Miṭṭa* and 894. *megha* mean "to sprinkle" and "to injure. 901. *ubundir* in the sense of perceiving (*niśāmana*). 902. *veṭ* in the senses of motion, knowledge, thought, perceiving, and grasping musical instruments; this root also ends in *n*. 903. *khanu* in the sense of digging or splitting open (*avadāraṇa*). 904. *cīvṛ* in the senses of taking up and covering. 905. *cāya* in the senses of worship and perceiving. 906. *vyaya* in the sense of going. 907. *dāṭa* in the sense of giving. 908. *bheṣa* in the sense of fear; some say it means "going. 909. *śreṣu* and 910. *bhleṣū* in the sense of going. 911. *asa* in the senses of going, shining, and taking; some say it is *aṣa*. 912. *spaśa* in the senses of harassing and touching.

913. *laṣ* in the sense of longing; 914. *caṣ* in the sense of eating; 915. *jhaṣ* in the senses of seizing and covering; 916. *chaṣ* in the sense of injury; 917. *bhrakṣ* and 918. *bhlakṣ* in the sense of eating; 919. *dāsa* in the sense of giving; 920. *māha* in the sense of measuring; 921. *guhū* in the sense of concealing. 947–8248. *ṣṇai* in the sense of "to wrap" (*veṣṭana*). [Roots] belonging to the *bhvādi* class; some say it is also used in the sense of "beauty" (*śobhā*). 949. *daip* in the sense of "purifying" (*śodhana*). 950. *pā* in the sense of "drinking" (*pāna*). 951. *ghrā* in the sense of "perceiving odor" (*gandhopādāna*). 952. *dhmā* in the senses of "sound" (*śabda*) and "contact with fire" (*agnisaṃyoga*). 953. *ṣṭhā* in the sense of "cessation of motion" (*gatinivṛtti*). 954. *mnā* in the sense of "repetition" (*abhyāsa*). 955. *dāṇ* in the sense of "giving" (*dāna*). 956. *vṛ* in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilya*). 957. *svṛ* in the senses of "sound" (*śabda*) and "affliction" (*upatāpa*). 958. *smṛ* in the sense of "thinking" (*cintā*). 959. *hṛ* in the sense of "concealment" (*saṃvaraṇa*). 960. *sṛ* in the sense of "motion" (*gati*). 961. *ṛ* in the senses of "motion" (*gati*) and "attaining" (*prāpaṇa*). 962. *gṛ* 963. *dhṛ* in the sense of "sprinkling" (*secana*).

964. *vah* (vaha) in the sense of carrying. 965. *sru* in the sense of going. 966. *ṣu* in the senses of procreation and sovereignty. 967. *śru* in the sense of hearing. 968. *dhru* in the sense of stability. 969. *ḍhu*. 970. *hru* in the sense of going. 971. *ji*. 972. *jri* in the sense of overcoming. The roots beginning with *dhayati* are anudātta and parasmaipada. 973. *ṣmiṅ* in the sense of smiling slightly. 974. *guḍū* in the sense of indistinct sound. 975. *gāḍū* in the sense of going. 976. *kuṅ*. 977. *ghuṅ*. 978. *uṅ*. 979. *ḍuṅ* in the sense of sound. Others say: *u*, *kuṅ*, *khaṅ*, *guṅ*, *ghuṅ*, *ḍhuṅ*.

980 *cyuṅ* (to fall); 981 *jyuṅga* (to go); 982 *muṅ* (to go); 983 *laṅ* (to go)—some say [it means] "river"; 984 *ruṅ* (in the senses of going and seeking); 985 *dhṛṅ* (in the sense of destroying); 986 *me* (in the sense of giving a jewel); 987 *de* (in the sense of protecting); 988 *śyaiṅ* (in the sense of going); 989 *pyaiṅ* (in the sense of increasing); 990 *traiṅ* (in the sense of protecting). The [roots] beginning with *udātta* are spoken in the *parasmaipada*. 995 *gup* (to hide); 996 *tij* (to sharpen); 997 *māna* (to honor); 998 *vadha* (to bind). The roots beginning with *skandi* are accented on the first syllable (*udātta*) and are conjugated in the *parasmaipada*. 1004. *skandir* (to move, to dry up) 1005. *yabh* (in sexual intercourse) 1006. *ṇam* (in greatness and sound) 1007. *gaml* (to go) 1008. *sapl* (to go) 1009. *yam* (to cease, to restrain) 1010. *tap* (to heat, to torment) 1011. *tyaj* (to abandon, to give up) 1012. *sañj* (to adhere, to cling) 1013. *dṛśir* (to see, to perceive) 1014. *daṃś* (to bite) 1015. *kṛṣ* (to scratch, to furrow) 1016. *dah* (to burn, to reduce to ashes) 1017. *miha* (to sprinkle, to moisten)

The roots *skanda* and others are anudātta (unaccented) and are marked with an udātta (acute) accent on their final vowel; they are conjugated in the Parasmaipada (active voice). 1018. *kita* (to dwell, and to remove disease): This is an udātta root and is conjugated in the Parasmaipada. 1019. *dāna* (to cut): 1020. *śāna* (to sharpen): These two are udātta roots and are conjugated in both voices (Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada). 1021. *hu-pacaṣ* (to cook): 1022. *ṣaca* (to assemble): 1023. *bhaja* (to serve): 1024. *rañja* (to color/attach): 1025. *śapa* (to curse): 1026. *tviṣa* (to shine): 1027. *yaja* (to worship the gods, to associate with, and to give): These are svarita (circumflex) roots and are conjugated in both voices.

1028. *dru* (to run): used in the sense of the continuity of seeds, even when there is cutting. 1029. *vaha* (to carry): [this root is] included among those beginning with *pac*. Those that have an indicatory vowel *ṅ* (anudātta) are marked with a svarita accent and are spoken of as being used in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*). However, *ṣaci* has an indicatory vowel *u* (udātta). 1030. *vas* (to dwell): [this root is] anudātta and udātta-it, and is spoken of in the parasmaipada voice. 1031. *veñ* (to weave): in the sense of the continuous extension of a thread. 1032. *vyeñ* (to cover/conceal). 1033. *hveñ* (to call out/invite): in the sense of rivalry and sound. These three, beginning with *veñ*, are anudātta and are spoken of in both voices. 1034. *vad* (to speak): in the sense of distinct speech. 1035. *ṭuośvi* (to move/grow): in the senses of motion and increase.

[The root] *vṛt*: these two, *vad* and *cit*, are *parasmaipada* [verbs] with initial *ā*. Thus end the *bhvādi* roots with *śap* conjugation. **Root List (Dhātupāṭha):** 1. *ad* in the sense of eating (*bhakṣaṇe*). 2. *han* in the senses of injury (*hiṃsā*) and motion (*gati*). These two are *anudātta* [roots], followed by an *udātta* vowel, and are *parasmaipada*. 3. *dviṣ* in the sense of hatred (*amītau*). 4. *duh* in the sense of milking/filling (*mapūraṇe*). 5. *diha* in the sense of accumulation (*upacaye*). 6. *liha* in the sense of tasting (*āsvāda*). These roots beginning with *dviṣ* are *anudātta*, have a *svarita* accent on the final syllable, and are *ubhayatobhāṣā* (conjugated in both *parasmaipada* and *ātmanepada*). 7. *cakṣiṅ* in the sense of distinct speech (*vyaktāyāṃ vāci*) and also seeing (*darśane*).

An unaccented (anudātta) root that takes the ātmanepada endings when followed by an unaccented (anudātta) affix [is udātta]. 8. *īr* in the sense of motion and trembling. 9. *īḍ* in the sense of praise. 10. *īś* in the sense of sovereignty. 11. *ās* in the sense of sitting. 12. *śās* with the prefix *āṅ* in the sense of desiring. 13. *vas* in the sense of covering. 14. *kas* in the sense of motion and teaching; some say *kasa*, others say *kaś*. 15. *ṇis* in the sense of kissing. 16. *ṇij* in the sense of purification. 17. *śin* in the sense of inarticulate sound. 18. *pij* in the sense of color; some say "in the sense of contact," others say "in both senses," and others say "in the sense of a part."

"Avyakta" (inarticulate) and "śabda" (sound)—thus say others; some say "pūji" (to honor). 19. *Vṛkṣī* (to avoid); others say *vṛṇi*. 20. *Pūcī* (to join together). The roots beginning with *īṅ* are udātta, anudāttet, and ātmanepadī. 21. *Ṣūṅ* (to release the vital breath or the fetus). 22. *Śī* (to sleep). These two are udātta and ātmanepadī. 23. *Yu* (to mix and not to mix). 24. *Ru* (to sound). 25. *Ṇu* (to praise). 26. *Kṣu* (to sound). 27. *Kṣṇu* (to sharpen). 28. *Ṣṇu* (to flow).

The roots beginning with *dyu* are udātta (accented) and, being udāttet (having an udātta vowel as their it), they are parasmaipada (active voice). 30. *ūrṇuñ* in the sense of covering; it is udātta and ubhayatobhāṣa (used in both voices). 31. *dyu* in the sense of approaching. 32. *pu* in the sense of procreation and sovereignty. 33. *kuśa* in the sense of sound. 34. *ṣṭuñ* in the sense of praising. The roots beginning with *hi* are anudātta (unaccented) and parasmaipada; *stu*, however, is ubhayatobhāṣa. 35. *brūñ* in the sense of distinct speech; it is udātta and ubhayatobhāṣa. 36. *iṇ* in the sense of motion. 37. *iṅ* in the sense of studying. 38. *ik* in the sense of remembering.

38. *vī* is used in the senses of going, pervading, conceiving, and eating. 39. *yā* is used in the sense of measuring. 40. *vā* is used in the senses of going and scenting. 41. *bhā* is used in the sense of shining. 42. *ṣṇā* is used in the sense of cleansing. 43. *śrā* is used in the sense of cooking. 44. *drā* is used in the sense of loathing and going. 45. *psā* is used in the sense of eating. 46. *pā* is used in the sense of protecting. 47. *rā* is used in the sense of giving. 48. *lā* is used in the sense of taking; both [roots] are also used in the sense of giving, according to Candra. 49. *dāp* is used in the sense of cutting. 50. *khyā* is used in the sense of narration. 51. *mā* is used in the sense of filling. 52. *mā* is used in the sense of measuring. 53. *vac* is used in the sense of speaking.

The roots beginning with *iṇ* are *anudātta* (unaccented) and *parasmaipadī* (active voice). However, *iṅ* is *ātmanepadī* (middle voice). 54. *vid* in the sense of knowing. 55. *as* in the sense of being. 56. *mṛj* in the sense of purification. 57. *rudir* in the sense of shedding tears. The roots beginning with *vid* are *udātta* (accented), have an *udātta* indicatory vowel (*udāttet*), and are *parasmaibhāṣā*. 58. *triṣvap* in the sense of sleeping. This is *udātta* and *parasmaibhāṣā*. 59. *śvasa* in the sense of breathing. 60. And *ana*. 61. *nakṣa* in the senses of eating and laughing. *Vṛt* (the section on these roots is concluded). 62. *jāgṛ* in the sense of the cessation of sleep. 63. *daridrā* in the sense of being in a bad state. 64. *cakāsṛ* in the sense of shining.

65. *Śās* in the sense of instruction. 9. *hudāñ* in the sense of giving (*dāne*). 10. *hudhā* in the senses of holding and nourishing (*dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); some also say it means "to lead" (*neti*). *udātta* (19) is *parasmaipada*. *ki* (20), meaning "to know," is *anudātta* and *parasmaipada*. *tura* (21), meaning "to hasten"; *dhiṣa* (22), meaning "in sound"; *dhana* (23), meaning "in grain"; *jana* (24), meaning "in birth. *Tura* and the others are *udātta*, and being *udātta*, they are spoken with the *parasmaipada* endings. *gā* (25), meaning "in praise," is *anudātta* and spoken with the *parasmaipada* endings. The eleven roots beginning with *ghṛ* are used in the Vedic language (*chandas*). *Iyarti* is also used in the common language (*bhāṣā*). Thus end the *juhotyādi* roots characterized by the *ślu* suffix.

1. *dinu* [is used] in the senses of playing, desiring victory, transacting, shining, praising, rejoicing, intoxication, sleeping, and moving with grace. 2. *ṣivu* [is used] in the sense of weaving or stringing together. 3. *ṣṭriṣu* [is used] in the senses of going and drying up. 4. *ṣṭhivu* [is used] in the sense of spitting out. 5. *ṣṇusu* [is used] in the sense of eating; some say in the sense of taking; others say in the sense of not seeing. 6. *ṣṇūsu* [is used] in the sense of spitting out. 7. *krusu* [is used] in the senses of seizing and shining. 8. *vyuṣa* [is used] in the sense of burning. 9. *laṣa* also [has this meaning]. 10. *nṛtī* [is used] in the sense of shaking the limbs (dancing). 11. *trasī* [is used] in the sense of agitation or fear. 12. *kutha* [is used] in the sense of becoming putrid. 13. *putha* [is used] in the sense of harming.

14. *guth* (to wrap); 15. *kṣip* (in the sense of throwing); 16. *puṣpa* (to blossom); 17. *tima*, 18. *ṣṭima*, 19. *ṣṭīma* (in the sense of becoming moist); 20. *brīḍ* (in the sense of urging and also shame); 21. *iṣ* (to go); 22. *ṣaha*, 23. *ṣuha* (in the sense of being able); 24. *juṣ*, 25. *jhūṣ* (in the sense of the decay of age). However, *kṣip* is anudātta. 26. *ṣu* (in the sense of procreation); 27. *dūṅ* (in the sense of tormenting)—these two are udātta and ātmanepada. 28. *dīṅ* (in the sense of wasting away).

29. *ḍīṅ* (ḍī) in the sense of moving through the air. 30. *dhīṅ* (dhī) in the sense of supporting. 31. *mīḍū* (mīḍ) in the sense of harming. 32. *rī* (rī) in the sense of hearing. 33. *lī* (lī) in the sense of clinging. 34. *brīḍū* (brīḍ) in the sense of being bashful; [it belongs to] the *vṛt* class. The roots beginning with *svād* and ending with *dīṅ* are marked with an indicatory vowel *i* (*āditaḥ*). 35. *pīkū* (pī) in the sense of drinking. 36. *mā* (mā) in the sense of measuring. 37. *ī* (ī) in the sense of going. 38. *prīṅ* (prī) in the sense of delighting. The roots beginning with *ḍīṅ* are *ātmanepada*-forming and have anudātta accents; *ḍīṅ* has an udātta accent. 39. *śo* (śo) in the sense of making thin. 40. *cho* (cho) in the sense of cutting. 41. *ṣo* (ṣo) in the sense of finishing. 42. *do* (do) in the sense of breaking off.

The following roots, beginning with *iya*, are anudātta (unaccented) and belong to the Parasmaipada (active voice). 43. *janī* in the sense of manifestation (*prādurbhāva*). 44. *dīpī* in the sense of shining (*dīpti*). 45. *pūrī* in the sense of filling (*āpyāyana*). 46. *tūrī* in the senses of motion (*gati*), hastening (*tvaraṇa*), and injury (*hiṃsana*). 47. *dhūrī*. 48. *gūrī* in the senses of injury (*hiṃsā*) and motion (*gati*). 49. *ghūrī*. 50. *jūrī* in the senses of injury (*hiṃsā*) and loss of vitality (*vayahāni*). 51. *śūra* in the senses of injury (*hiṃsā*) and paralysis/stiffness (*stambhana*). 52. *cūrī* in the sense of burning (*dāha*). 53. *tapa* in the sense of sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), or [in the sense of heating]. 54. *vṛtu* in the sense of choosing (*varaṇa*). 55. *kiśa* in the sense of affliction (*upatāpa*). 56. *kāśa* in the sense of shining (*dīpti*). 57. *vāṭa* in the sense of sound (*śabda*).

The roots beginning with *jani* are accented acute (*udātta*), belong to the *anudāttet* class, and are conjugated in the middle voice (*ātmanepadī*). However, *tap* is accented grave (*anudātta*). 58. *mṛṣ* in the sense of endurance (*titikṣā*). 59. *śuci* in the sense of becoming pure (*pūtībhāva*). Some say *śvaṭhi*. (33) *tuni* (34) *pini* [mean] injury, taking by force, and dwelling. Some say *tuja* and *pija*. Some say *laji* and *luji*. (35) *pisa* means "to go. (36) *ṣāntva* means "the employment of conciliation. (37) *ivalka* (38) *valka* mean "to speak around" or "to address. (39) *ṇiha* means "to moisten. Some say *sphiṭa*. (40) *miṭa* means "disrespect. Some say *bhiṅ*. (41) *śliṣa* means "to embrace" or "to adhere. (42) *pathi* means "to go. (43) *piccha* means "to strike" or "to cut. (44) *chadi* means "to cover. (45) *śraṇa* means "to give."

46. *taḍ* in the sense of striking. 47. *khaḍ* 48. *khaḍi* 49. *kaḍi* in the sense of breaking. 50. *kuḍi* in the sense of protecting; some say "in the sense of protecting," others say *kuṭhi*, and still others say *guṭhi*. 51. *guḍi* in the sense of encircling. 52. *khuḍi* in the sense of splitting. 53. *vāṭa* in the sense of dividing; some read *vaḍi*. 54. *maḍi* in the sense of adorning and joy. 55. *bhahi* in the sense of auspiciousness. 56. *charda* in the sense of vomiting. 57. *pusta* 58. *busta* in the senses of respect and disrespect. 59. *cuda* in the sense of inciting. 60. *naka* 61. *dhaka* in the sense of destroying.

62. *caka* (63. *cuka*), in the sense of pain; 64. *kṣala*, in the sense of the act of cleansing; 65. *tala*, in the sense of establishing; 66. *tula*, in the sense of measuring; 67. *dula*, in the sense of lifting up; 68. *pula*, in the sense of greatness; 69. *cula*, in the sense of height; 70. *mūla*, in the sense of growing; 71. *kala* (72. *vila*), in the sense of throwing; 73. *bila*, in the sense of splitting; 74. *tila*, in the sense of oiliness; 75. *cala*, in the sense of maintenance; 76. *pāla*, in the sense of protecting; 77. *lūṣa*, in the sense of injury; 78. *śulba*, in the sense of measuring; 79. and *jūrpa*; 80. *cuṭa*, in the sense of cutting.

81. *muṭha* in the sense of crushing; 82. *paḍi* and 83. *pasi* in the sense of destruction; 84. *vaja* in the sense of path-preparation and motion; 85. *śulka* in the sense of excessive touching; 86. *capi* in the sense of motion; 87. *kṣapi* in the sense of forbearance; 88. *chaji* in the sense of living with difficulty; 89. *varta* in the sense of motion; 90. and also *śvana*; 91. *jñapa* in the senses of knowing, causing to know, killing, pleasing, sharpening, and quieting. Some say [it takes] *mit* [as its class marker]. 92. *yama* also in the sense of serving food; 93. *caha* in the sense of deceit; some say *capa*. 94. *raha* in the sense of abandonment as well.

95. *vala* in the sense of measuring; 96. *ciñ* in the sense of gathering (*caya*). No other [roots] beginning with a *mit* vowel [are included] when not preceded by a prefix (*ahetau*). 97. *ghaṭṭa* in the sense of moving; 98. *musta* in the sense of a collection (*saṃghāta*); 99. *khaṭṭa* in the sense of covering (*saṃvaraṇa*); 100. *ṣaṭṭa*; 101. *sphiṭṭa*; 102. *cubi* in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*); 103. *pūla* in the sense of a collection (*saṃvāta*). Some say [the root is] *pūrṇa*; others say [it is] *pūrṇa*. 104. *puṃsa* in the sense of increasing (*abhivardhana*); 105. *ṭaki* in the sense of binding (*bandhana*); 106. *dhūsa* in the sense of making beautiful (*kāntikaraṇa*). 146. *matri* (to conceal, to reproach). 147. *spaś* (to seize, to touch). 148. *tarja* (to threaten). 149. *bhartsa* (to revile, to threaten). 150. *vasta* (to injure). 151. *gandha* (to injure). 152. *viṣka* (to injure); some say it is *hiṣka*. 153. *niṣka* (to measure). 154. *lala* (to desire). 155. *kaṇa* (to contract). 156. *tūṇa* (to fill). 157. *bhrūṇa* (hope and apprehension). 158. *śaṭa* (to deceive). 159. *yakṣa* (to worship). 160. *syama* (to conjecture). 161. *gura* (to exert oneself).

162. *śama* (to be calm); 163. *lakṣa* (in the sense of observing/perceiving); 164. *kutsa* (in the sense of reviling); 165. *truṭa* (in the sense of cutting). Some say [the root] *kuṭa* [is used here]. 166. *gala* (in the sense of flowing); 167. *bhala* (in the sense of mocking/ridiculing); 168. *kūṭa* (in the sense of deceiving). Some say [it means] "in the sense of causing dejection. 169. *kuṭṭa* (in the sense of tormenting); 170. *vañcu* (in the sense of deceiving); 171. *vṛṣa* (in the sense of impotence/incapacity); 172. *mada* (in the sense of satiety/satisfaction); 173. *dibu* (in the sense of warbling/cooing); 174. *gṛ* (in the sense of perceiving/knowing); 175. *vida* (in the sense of consciousness, narration, and distribution).

176. *māna* in the sense of pride; 177. *yu* in the sense of loathing; 178. *kusma* optionally [denotes] the name of one who smiles contemptuously. These are the *āk-kusmīya* roots. 179. *carca* in the sense of study; 180. *bukka* in the sense of barking; 181. *śabda*, when preceded by a prefix, also in the sense of making manifest; 182. *kaṇa* in the sense of closing the eyes; 183. *jabhi* in the sense of destruction; 184. *ṣūḍh* in the sense of flowing; 185. *jasu* in the sense of striking; 186. *paśu* in the sense of binding; 187. *am* in the sense of freedom from disease; 188. *caṭa* and 189. *sphuṭa* in the sense of splitting; 190. *vaṭa* in the sense of covering, and those having the meaning of "to kill."

191. *div* in the sense of crushing (*mardana*). 192. *arja* in the sense of acquisition (*pratiyatna*). 193. *ghuṣi* in the sense of making a sound (*viśabdana*). 194. *āṅ-pūrva krand* in the sense of continuity (*sātatya*). 195. *lasa* in the sense of application to an art (*śilpayoga*). 196. *tasi*. 197. *bhūṣa* in the sense of adorning (*alaṃkaraṇa*). 198. *arha* in the sense of honoring (*pūjā*). 199. *jñā* in the sense of command (*niyoga*). 200. *bhaja* in the sense of bestowing (*viśrāṇana*). 201. *śṛdhu* in the sense of enduring (*asahana*). 202. *yata* in the sense of contempt (*nikāra*) and improvement (*upaskāra*). 203. *aka*. 204. *laga* in the sense of tasting (*āsvādana*). 206. *ligi* in the sense of making a mark or painting. 207. *muda* in the sense of contact or union. 208. *nasa* in the sense of holding; some say "in the sense of grasping," others say "in the sense of warding off. 209. *udhasa* in the sense of gathering or picking up; some say the letter *u* is part of the root, others say it is not. 210. *muca* in the sense of releasing or gladdening. 211. *vasa* in the senses of affection, cutting, and taking away. 212. *cara* in the sense of doubt. 213. *cyu* in the sense of enduring; some say also "in the sense of laughing"; some say the root is *cyus*. 214. *bhuva* in the sense of reflecting or deliberating. 215. And [the rule applies] after *kṛp*. Up to the root *svad*, [the suffix *san* is added] when the root is transitive.

216. *grasa* in the sense of seizing; 217. *puṣa* in the sense of supporting; 218. *dala* in the sense of splitting; 219. *paṭa*, 220. *puṭa*, 221. *luṭa*, 222. *tuni*, 223. *mini*, 224. *pini*, 225. *liji*, 226. *luji*, 227. *bhani*, 228. *lāye*, 229. *trasi*, 230. *pisi*, 231. *kusi*, 232. *daśi* (58). [End of] the Dhātupāṭha.

232 *kuśi*, 233 *ghaṭa*, 234 *ghaṭi*, 235 *vṛhi*, 236 *varha*, 237 *vahna*, 238 *gup*, 239 *dhūp*, 240 *vicch*, 241 *cīv*, 242 *puth*, 243 *lok*, 244 *lovṛ*, 245 *pad*, 246 *kup*, 247 *tark*, 248 *vṛt*, 249 *vṛdh*—these have the sense of speaking (*bhāṣārtha*). 250 *ruṭ*, 251 *lajj*, 252 *añj*, 253 *daṃs*, 254 *bhṛś*, 255 *ruś*, 256 *śīk*, 257 *rus*, 258 *naṭ*, 259 *puṭ*, 260 *nij*, 261 *ci*, 262 *ragh*, 263 *lagh*, 264 *ah*, 265 *rah*, and 266 *mah* [have the sense of speaking].

267. *laḍhi* (to sport); 268. *taḍa* (to strike); 269. *nala* (to bind). 270. *pūrī* (in the sense of filling or satiating). 271. *ruja* (in the sense of injury). 272. *pvad* (in the sense of tasting); some say *svād*. [The roots] up to *dhṛṣ* are optional. 273. *yuja* and 274. *pṛca* (in the sense of restraining). 275. *arca* (in the sense of worship). 276. *ṣaha* (in the sense of enduring). 277. *īra* (in the sense of casting away). 278. *lī* (in the sense of liquefying). 279. *vṛnī* (in the sense of avoiding). 280. *vṛñ* (in the sense of covering). 281. *ju* (in the sense of decay of vitality); 282. *ji* (the same). 283. *rica* (in the sense of separation and mixing). 284. *śiṣa* (in the sense of not being used entirely).

285. *tapa* (to burn). 286. *tṛpa* (to satisfy); according to some, [it means] to kindle. 287. *hṛdī* (to kindle). According to some, *cupa*, *chupa*, and *dṛpa* [mean] to kindle. 288. *dṛbhī* (to fear). 289. *dṛbha* (to weave or compose). 290. *śratha* (to loosen); according to others, [it means] to injure. 291. *mī* (to go). 292. *grantha* (to bind). 293. *śīka* (to be impatient or to sprinkle). 294. *cauka* (and likewise). 295. *arda* (to injure); [this root is] svarita-accented. 296. *hiṃsi* (to injure). 297. *arha* (to worship or be worthy).

298. *āṅ* with *ṣad* in the sense of falling down (*padyarthe*). 299. *śundha* in the sense of cleansing (*śaucakarmaṇi*). 300. *chada* in the sense of covering (*apavāraṇe*); this root is *svarita*-accented. 301. *juṣa* in the sense of deliberation (*paritarkaṇe*); others say in the sense of satisfying (*paritarpaṇe*). 302. *dhūñ* in the sense of shaking (*kampane*). 303. *mīñ* in the sense of satisfying (*tarpaṇe*). 304. *grantha*. 305. *grantha* in the sense of composition (*saṃdarbhe*). 306. *āpūla* in the sense of obtaining (*lambhane*). Some say this root is *svarita*-accented. 307. *tanu* in the sense of faith (*śraddhā*) and preparation (*upakaraṇa*). There is lengthening [of the vowel] due to a prefix (*upasarga*). Some say [it means] non-faith (*aśraddhā*) and injury (*upahanan*).

308. *Vad* (to speak) is used in the sense of delivering a message; it is *svarita*-accented, though some say it is *anudātta*. 309. *Vac* (to speak). 310. *Mān* (to honor). 311. *Bhū* (to obtain) is *ātmanepada*. 312. *Garh* (to censure). 313. *Mārg* (to search). 314. *Kaṭh* (to grieve). 315. *Mṛj* (to cleanse and to adorn). 316. *Mṛṣ* (to endure); it is *svarita*-accented. 317. *Dhṛṣ* (to dare). These are the roots beginning with *dhṛṣ*. Now follow those ending in short *a*: 318. *Kath* (to compose a discourse). 319. *Var* (to desire).

320. *gaṇ* in the sense of counting. 321. *śaṭha* and 322. *vaṭha* in the sense of speaking correctly. 323. *paṭa* and 324. *vaṭa* in the sense of binding. 325. *raha* in the sense of abandoning. 326. *stana* and 327. *gadī* in the sense of a divine sound. 328. *pata* in the sense of going; some say it is optionally vowel-ending (*adanta*). 329. *paṣa* when not preceded by a prefix. 330. *svara* in the sense of reviling. 331. *raca* in the sense of effort toward accomplishment. 332. *kala* in the sense of going and counting. 333. *caha* in the sense of deceit. 334. *maha* in the sense of worship.

335 *sāra* (to extract the essence), 336 *kṛpa* (to pity); then [the following are] in the sense of weakness. 337 *spṛha* (to desire). 338 *bhāma* (to be angry). 339 *sūca* (to slander). 340 *kheṭa* (to eat); some say it ends in the third case (*kheṭati*), others say *khoṭa*. 341 *kṣoṭa* (to throw away). 342 *goma* (to smear). 343 *kumāra* (to play). 344 *śīla* (to assume). 345 *sāma* (to employ conciliation). 346 *vela* (to indicate time); some say *kāla* is a separate root.

348. *palyūla* in the sense of winnowing and purifying. 349. *vāta* in the sense of pleasant service; some say it means "going" and "pleasant service. 350. *gaveṣa* in the sense of seeking. 351. *vāsa* in the sense of attending upon. 352. *nivāsa* in the sense of covering. The *curādigaṇa* (Class XIX). 353. *bhāja* in the sense of dividing. 354. *samāja* in the sense of seeing with affection; some say it means "affection" and "service. 355. *ūna* in the sense of diminishing. 356. *dhvana* in the sense of sound. 357. *kūṭa* in the sense of tormenting; others say it means "burning."

358 *saṅketa* (to agree upon); 359 *grāma* (to assemble); 360 *kuṇa* and 361 *guṇa* (in the sense of inviting); 362 *keta* (in the sense of causing to hear and inviting); 363 *kuṇa* (also in the sense of contracting); 364 *stena* (in the sense of stealing). From here up to the end [of this section], the roots are *ātmanepada*. 365 *padga* (in the sense of going); 366 *gṛha* (in the sense of seizing); 367 *mṛga* (in the sense of searching); 368 *kuha* (in the sense of astonishing); 369 *śūra* and 370 *cīra* (in the sense of valor); 371 *sthūla* (in the sense of increasing in bulk); 372 *artha* (in the sense of requesting); 373 *satra* (in the sense of the act of continuous performance).

374. *garv* (to be proud); thus ends the section on *āgavayāḥ*. 375. *sūtra* (to weave). 376. *mūtra* (to urinate). 377. *rūkṣa* (to be harsh). 378. *pāra*, 379. *tīra* (both meaning the completion of an action). 380. *puṭa* (to join together). 381. *dheka* (to see); some say [it means] "to see. 382. *katra* (to loosen); some also say *karta*. [The following is a rule: From a nominal stem (*prātipadika*), when the sense of a verbal root (*dhātvartha*) is intended, [the suffix *ṇic*] is applied diversely (*bahulam*), and it is treated like the suffix *iṣṭhan*. [Examples of its application are: "he does that" (*tat karoti*), "he describes that" (*tad ācaṣṭe*), or "he surpasses by means of that" (*tenātikrāmati*).

And the form of the verbal root (*dhātu*). From the rule "When one expresses that which was formed by a *kṛt* suffix, there is the restoration of the original root-form and the *kāraka* is as in the original" (*ākhyānātkṛtaḥ tadācaṣṭe kṛlṛchukprakṛtipratyāpattiḥ prakṛtivacca kārakam*), [the following roots are listed]: 383. *valka*, in the sense of seeing. 384. *citra*, in the sense of making variegated; sometimes in the sense of seeing. 385. *aṃsa*, in the sense of falling down. 386. *vaṭa*, in the sense of dividing. 387. *laja*, in the sense of manifesting. Some say *vaṭi* and *laji*. 388. *miśra*, in the sense of contact. 389. *saṃgrāma*, in the sense of fighting; this is *anudātta*-accented. 390. *stoma*, in the sense of praising.

391. *chid* (to pierce); [the root] *karṇa* means "piercing. Some say it means "instrumental piercing," while others maintain that *karṇa* is a separate verbal root. 392. *andha* (to become blind); [it means] "obscuration of vision. Others say it means "withdrawal. 393. *daṇḍ* (to inflict punishment); [it means] "the striking down of a staff. 394. *aṅk* (to mark); [it means] "a foot" and "a characteristic mark. 395. *aṅg* (also [means "to mark"]). 396. *sukha* (pleasure). 397. *duḥkha* (pain); [it means] "the action of producing that. 398. *ras* (to taste); [it means] "tasting" and "moistening. 399. *vyay* (to spend); [it means] "the relinquishing of wealth. 400. *rūp* (to form); [it means] "the act of forming. 401. *ched* (to cut); [it means] "making twofold" (dividing).

402. *chad* in the sense of covering (*apavāraṇe*). 403. *lābha* in the sense of inciting (*preraṇe*). 404. *vaṇa* in the sense of rubbing the limbs (*gātravicūrṇane*). 405. *varṇa* in the senses of coloring (*varṇakriyā*), expansion (*vistāra*), and speaking of qualities (*guṇavacana*). This is a frequent illustration [of such usage]. 406. *parṇa* in the sense of being green (*haritabhāve*). 407. *viṣka* in the sense of seeing (*darśane*). 408. *kṣapa* in the sense of dying (*maraṇe*). 409. *vasa* in the sense of dwelling (*nivāse*). 410. *tuttha* in the sense of covering (*āvaraṇe*). [The following are irregular forms: *ṅiṅga* in the sense of casting out (*nirasane*). In the case of *śvetāśva*, *aśvatara*, *ga*, *loḍita*, and *aharakāṇām*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the suffixes *-aśvatara* and *-etaka*.

In the case of *pṛcchā* and others, the meaning of the verbal root is already established by the nominal stem (*prātipadika*) itself. Thus ends [the section on] *ṇij*-affixes in their own sense (*svārthe*), including *ap*, *ur*, and so forth. The *Dhātupāṭha* composed by the venerable sage Pāṇini is hereby completed. **Instruction on Gender (*Liṅgānuśāsana*)** 1. Gender (*liṅga*). 2. Feminine (*strī*). 3. Words ending in long *ṛ* are feminine: *mātṛ* (mother), *duhitṛ* (daughter), *svasṛ* (sister), *potṛ* (father-in-law), and *nanāndṛ* (husband’s sister). 4. A verbal root (*dhātu*) ending in the suffix *ū* is feminine. 5. *Aśani* (thunderbolt), *bharaṇi* (a star), and *araṇi* (fire-drill) are masculine as well. 6. Words ending in the suffix *min* are feminine. 7. *Vahni* (fire), *vṛṣṇi* (a bull), and *amaya* (disease) are masculine. 8. *Śroṇi* (hip), *yoni* (womb), and *ūrmi* (wave) are masculine as well.

9. A word ending in *ktin* [is feminine]. 10. And one ending in *ikāra* (*i*) [is feminine]. 11. And one ending in *ūṅ*, *yāp*, or *āp* [is feminine]. 12. A monosyllabic word ending in *y* or *v* [is feminine]. 13. Words beginning with *viṃśati* up to *navati* [are feminine]. 14. *Dundubhi* is feminine when referring to drums. 15. *Nābhi* is feminine when not referring to a Kṣatriya. 16. Both [the preceding two] are masculine elsewhere. 17. A word ending in *tal* [is feminine]. 18. Words denoting earth, lightning, a river, a creeper, and a woman [are feminine]. 19. *Yādas* (water-monsters) is neuter. 20. *Bhās*, *nu*, *kstrā*, *diś*, *guṣṇih*, and *upānah* [are feminine]. 21. *Sthūṇā* and *ūrṇā* are also neuter. 22. [The words] *gṛha* and *śas* are neuter.

23. *māvṛḍḍimaḍruṭūḍitviṣaḥ* (the words *mā*, *vṛt*, *ḍima*, *ḍruṭ*, *ḍit*, and *tviṣ* [are feminine]). 24. *darvividivedikhaniśāṇyabhriveśikṛṣyoṣadhikaṭyadgulayaḥ* (the words *darvi*, *vidi*, *vedi*, *khani*, *śāṇī*, *abhri*, *veśī*, *kṛṣi*, *oṣadhi*, *kaṭi*, *adyat*, and *gulī* [are feminine]). 25. *tithināḍiru cavīcinālidhūlikikikelicchavirājyādayaḥ* (the words beginning with *tithi*, *nāḍī*, *ruc*, *vīci*, *nāli*, *dhūli*, *kiki*, *eli*, *chavi*, and *rājī* [are feminine]). 26. *śaṣkulirājikuṣyaśanivartibhrukuṭitruṭivalipaṅkayaḥ* (the words *śaṣkulī*, *rājī*, *kuṣī*, *aśani*, *varti*, *bhrukuṭi*, *truṭi*, *vali*, and *paṅkti* [are feminine]). 27. *pratipadāpadvipatsaṃpaccharatsaṃsatpāriṣaduṣaḥsaṃvitkṣudyunmutsamidhaḥ* (the words *pratipad*, *āpad*, *vipad*, *saṃpad*, *śarat*, *saṃsat*, *pāriṣad*, *uṣas*, *saṃvit*, *kṣudh*, *yudh*, *mudh*, and *samidh* [are feminine]). 28. *āśīḥ-pūraḥ* (the word *āśis* ending in *ṣ* and the word *pūra* [are feminine]). 29. *apsumanassamāsikatāvarṣāṇāṃ bahutvaṃ ca* (the words *ap*, *sumanas*, *samit*, *sikatā*, and *varṣā* [are feminine] and they may also take the plural number).

30. *Sruk*, *tvak*, *ajagmā*, *yavānuga*, *auṣṭhika*, and *sphic* [are feminine]. 31. Words ending in *taṭi*, *sīman*, and *saṃvadhya* [are feminine]. 32. *Cūlli*, *veṇī*, and *khārī* [are feminine]. 33. *Tārā*, *dhārā*, *jyotsnā*, and others [are feminine]. 34. *Śalākā* is always feminine. 1. [The following] are masculine: 2. Those ending in the suffix *ghañ*. 3. And those ending in the suffix *gha*. 4. The words *bhaya*, *liṅga*, and *bhaga* are neuter. 5. Those ending in the suffix *naṅ* [are neuter]. 6. *Yācyā* is feminine. 7. A verbal root (*dhātu*) ending in the suffix *ky* [is feminine].

8. *iṣudhi* (quiver) is feminine. 9. Words denoting gods, asuras, self, heaven, mountain, ocean, nail, hair, tooth, breast, arm, neck, sword, arrow, and mud [are masculine]. 10. *triviṣṭapa* and *tribhuvana* are neuter. 11. *dyauḥ* (heaven) is feminine. 12. *iṣu* (arrow) and *bāhu* (arm) are also feminine. 13. *bāṇa* and *kāṇḍa* are also neuter. 14. [Words] ending in *n* [are masculine]. 15. Words denoting season (*ṛtu*), man (*puruṣa*), cheek (*kapola*), ankle (*gulpha*), and ram (*meṣa*) [are masculine]. 16. *abhra* (cloud) is neuter. 17. [Words] ending in the vowel *u* [are masculine].

18. *dhenu*, *rajju*, *kuhu*, *sarayu*, *tanu*, *reṇu*, and *priyaṅgu* are feminine. 19. In a compound, *rajju* may also be masculine. 20. *śmaśru*, *jānu*, *svādhiḥ*, *śru*, *jatu*, *trapu*, and *tālu* are neuter. 21. *Vasu* is neuter when it signifies "wealth. 22. *madgu*, *madhu*, *śīdhu*, *sānu*, and *kamaṇḍalu* are also neuter. 23. Words ending in *r* [are neuter]. 24. *Dāru*, *kaseru*, *jatru*, *vastu*, and *mastu* are neuter. 25. *Saktu* is also neuter. 26. Up to the word *raśmi*, words ending in *a* [are neuter]. 27. A word having *k* as its penultimate letter [is neuter].

28. *cibuka*, *śālūka*, *prātipadika*, *aṃśuka*, and *ulmuka* are neuter. 29. *kaṇṭaka*, *anīka*, *saraka*, *modaka*, *caṣaka*, *mastaka*, *pustaka*, *taḍāka*, *niṣka*, *śuṣka*, *varcaska*, *pināka*, *bhāṇḍaka*, *kaṭaka*, *daṇḍaka*, *piṭaka*, *tālakā*, *phalaka*, *kalka*, and *pulāka* are neuter, [and masculine]. 30. A word ending in *ṭa* [is neuter]. 31. *kirīṭa*, *mukuṭa*, *lalāṭa*, *vaṭa*, *vīṭa*, *śṛṅgāṭaka*, *raṭa*, and *lāṣṭa* are neuter. 32. *kuṭa*, *kūṭa*, *kapaṭa*, *kapāṭa*, *karpaṭa*, *naṭa*, *nikaṭa*, *kīṭa*, and *kaṭa* are neuter, [and masculine].

33. A word with *ṇ* as its penultimate letter [is neuter]. 34. *Ṛṇa*, *lavaṇa*, *parṇa*, *toraṇa*, *raṇa*, and *uṣṇa* are neuter. 35. *Kārṣāpaṇa*, *svarṇa*, *muvarṇa*, *vaṇa*, *caraṇa*, *vṛṣaṇa*, *viṣāṇa*, *cūrṇa*, and *tṛṇa* are also neuter. 36. A word with *th* as its penultimate letter [is neuter]. 37. *Kāṣṭha*, *pṛṣṭha*, *riktha*, and *uktha* are neuter. 38. *Kāṣṭhā*, when meaning "direction," is feminine. 39. *Tīrtha*, *protha*, *yūtha*, and *gāthā* are also neuter. 40. A word with *n* as its penultimate letter [is neuter].

41. Words ending in *javana*, *ajina*, *tuhina*, *kānana*, *vana*, *vṛjana*, *vipina*, *vetasa*, *śāsana*, *sopāna*, *mithuna*, *śmaśāna*, *ratna*, *nimna*, and *cihna* are neuter. 42. The *liṅgānuśāsana* (treatise on gender) for words ending in *māna*, *yāna*, *abhidhāna*, *nalina*, *pulina*, *udyāna*, *śayana*, *āsana*, *sthāna*, *candana*, *ālāna*, *saṃmāna*, *bhavana*, *vasana*, *vibhāvana*, and *vimāna* is that they are neuter; and [they are also masculine]. 43. [Words] having *ṣ* as their penultimate letter (*ṣopadha*). 44. Words ending in *pāpa*, *rūpa*, *uḍupa*, *talpa*, *śilpa*, *puṣpa*, *śaṣpa*, *samapa*, and *antarīpa* are neuter.

45. Words ending in *śūrpa*, *kutapa*, *kuṇapa*, *dvīpa*, and *viṭapa* are neuter; and [words] ending in a nasal (*na*) are also neuter. 46. A word with *bh* as its penultimate letter (*bhopadha*) is [neuter]. 47. *Talabha* is neuter. 48. *Jṛmbha* is also neuter. 49. A word with *m* as its penultimate letter (*mopadha*) is [neuter]. 50. *Rukma*, *sidhma*, *yugma*, *edhma*, *gulma*, *ādhyātma*, and *kuṅkuma* are neuter. 51. *Saṃgrāma*, *dāḍima*, *kusuma*, *āśrama*, *kṣema*, *kṣauma*, *homa*, and *uddāma* are also neuter. 52. A word with *y* as its penultimate letter (*yopadha*) is [neuter]. 53. *Kisalaya*, *hṛdaya*, *indriya*, and *uttarīya* are neuter.

54. Words ending in *gomaya*, *kaṣāya*, *malaya*, *anvaya*, and *avyaya* are neuter; and [the word] *roṣadha*. 55. *Dvāra*, *agra*, *sphāra*, *takra*, *vaktra*, *makṣika*, *kṣudra*, *chidra*, *nīra*, *tīra*, *dūra*, *kṛcchra*, *randhra*, *aśra*, *aśvabhra*, *bhīra*, *gabhīra*, *krūra*, *vicitra*, *keyūra*, *kedāra*, *udara*, *śarīra*, *kandara*, *mandara*, *pañjara*, *ajara*, *jaṭhara*, *ajira*, *avaira*, *cāmara*, *puṣkara*, *gahvara*, *kuṭīra*, *kulīra*, *catvara*, *kāśmīra*, *nīra*, *ambara*, *śiśira*, *tantra*, *yantra*, *kṣetra*, *kṣatra*, *mitra*, *kala*, *vaccha*—[these are masculine].

The following words ending in *tras*, *sūtra*, *vaktra*, *netra*, *gotra*, *aṅguli*, *tratra*, *bha*, *latra*, *astra*, *śastra*, *śāstra*, *vastra*, *patra*, *pātra*, and *nakṣatra* are neuter. (57) *Śukra* [is masculine] when it means a deity. (58) *Cakra*, *vajra*, *andhakāra*, *sāra*, *āvāra*, *pāra*, *kṣīra*, *tomara*, *śṛṅgāra*, *bhṛṅgāra*, *mandāra*, *uśīra*, *timira*, and *śiśira* are neuter, and [masculine as well]. (59) A word having *ṣ* as its penultimate letter [is neuter]. (60) *Śirīṣa*, *joṣa*, *ambarīṣa*, *pīyūṣa*, *purīṣa*, *kalbiṣa*, and *kalmāṣa* are neuter. (61) *Yūṣa*, *karīṣa*, *miṣa*, *viṣa*, and *varṣa* are neuter, and [masculine as well].

62. *Sopadha* [is masculine]. 63. *Pañca*, *na*, *sa*, *bi*, *su*, *sa*, and *sāhasa* are neuter. 64. *Camasa*, *sarasa*, *niryāsa*, *upavāsa*, *karpāsa*, *vāsa*, *māsa*, *kāsa*, *kāṃsa*, and *māṃsa* are [neuter] and [masculine]. 65. *Kaṃsa* is also [neuter] when it does not refer to a living being. 66. Words denoting rays and days [are masculine]. 67. *Dīdhiti* is feminine. 68. *Dina* and *ahana* are neuter. 69. Words denoting measures [of capacity] [are masculine]. 70. *Droṇa* and *āḍhaka* are [masculine] and [neuter]. 71. *Khārī* and *mānika* are feminine. 72. *Dāra*, *akṣata*, *lāja*, and *asūn* also take the plural.

73. Words for wounds (*vraṇa*), limbs (*aṅga*), and feet (*pada*) do not take the suffixes *nāṅya*, *apaja*, and *upapada*. 74. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *marut*, *garut*, *uttara*, and *ṛtvij*. 75. After a seer’s name (*ṛṣi*), [the suffix *ini* is applied] to express a blessing (*āśis*), a season (*ṛtu*), a knot (*granthi*), a worm (*krimi*), sound (*dhvani*), an offering (*bali*), a crest (*mauli*), a sun-stone (*ravi*), and a sage (*muni*). 76. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *dhvaja*, *gaja*, *muñja*, and *puñja*. 77. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *hasta*, *kunta*, *anta*, *vāta*, *dūta*, *dhūrta*, *sūta*, *cūta*, and *muhūrta*. 78. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *ṣaṇḍa*, *maṇḍa*, *karaṇḍa*, *bharaṇḍa*, *raṇḍa*, *varaṇḍa*, *tuṇḍa*, *gaṇḍa*, *muṇḍa*, *pāṣaṇḍa*, and *śikhaṇḍa*. 79. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *vaṃśa*, *aṃśa*, and *puroḍāśa*. 80. [The suffix *ini* is applied after] *hūda*, *kanda*, *kunda*, *bubuda*, and *śabda*.

81. *Arvāpatha*, *yyṛbhukṣi*, *stamba*, *nitamba*, and *pūga*; 82. *pallava*, *palvala*, *kaphara*, *repha*, *kaṭāha*, *nirvyūha*, *maṭha*, *maṇita*, *raṅga*, *gandha-skandha*, *mṛdaṅgha-saṅga*, and *samudra-puṃkha*; 83. *sārathi*, *atithi*, *kukṣi*, *vasti*, *pāṇi*, and *añjali*. 1. Neuter [nouns are formed by the suffixes mentioned below]. 2. A word ending in the suffix *lyuṭ* denotes an action (*bhāva*). 3. And the past passive participle suffixes (*niṣṭhā*) also denote an action. 4. The secondary suffixes (*taddhita*) *tva* and *aṇ* [denote an action]. 5. And [the suffix *aṇ*] is used in the sense of the object (*karman*) after words belonging to the *brāhmaṇa*-class and those expressing qualities (*guṇavacana*). 6. The suffixes *ya-yaṅ*, *gha-ghañ*, *aṇ*, *vuc*, and *chāś* [are used] in the sense of an action or an object.

7. An *avyayībhāva* compound is neuter. 8. A *dvandva* compound denoting a single entity is neuter. 9. In non-Vedic usage, *hemanta-śiśira-* and *ahorātra-* are neuter. 10. A *tatpuruṣa* compound that is not a negative (*nañ*) or a *karmadhāraya* is [neuter when ending in] *-am*. 11. *Chāyā* is neuter when it does not mean "much. 12. *Sabhā*, preceded by a word other than *rājan* or *amanuṣya*, is neuter. 13. *Surā*, *senā*, *chāyā*, *śālā*, and *niśā* are also feminine. 14. [The gender of a compound] follows that of the subsequent member (*paravat*). 15. Words ending in *rātra*, *ahan*, and *aha* are masculine. 16. *Apatha* and *puṇyāha* are neuter. 17. *Rātri* preceded by a numeral is neuter. 18. A *dvigu* compound is also feminine. 19. Words ending in *is* and *us* are neuter. 20. *Arcis* is also feminine.

21. *Chadiḥ* (roofing) is used only in the feminine. 22. Words denoting mouth, eye, iron, forest, flesh, blood, bow, hole, water, plough, wealth, and navel [are masculine]. 23. *Sīra*, *athada*, and *na* are masculine. 24. *Vaktra*, *netra*, *araṇya*, and *gāṇḍīva* are also masculine. 25. *Aṭavī* (forest) is feminine. 26. A word ending in *l* [is masculine]. 27. *Tula*, *upala*, *tāla*, *kusūla*, *tarala*, *kambala*, *devala*, and *vṛṣala* are masculine. 28. *Śīla*, *mūla*, and *aṅga*—this concludes the instruction on gender (*liṅgānuśāsana*).

29. *Lasāla*, *kamalatala*, *musala*, *kuṇḍala*, *palāla*, *mṛṇāla*, *vānīra*, *galābī*, and *khaḍga* [end in -a]. 30. Numbers beginning with *śata* (hundred) are [masculine]; *śata*, *ayuta*, and *mayuta* are also masculine. 31. *Lakṣā* and *koṭī* are feminine; *mahasra* is also masculine. 32. *Mandrayaka* is used when not denoting the agent. 33. *Brahman* is also masculine. 34. *Nāman* and *roman* are neuter. 35. Those ending in *-as* and *-ac* are [neuter]. 36. *Apsarāḥ* is feminine. 37. Those ending in *-ān* are [neuter]. 38. *Yātrā*, *mātrā*, and those ending in *bhakāra* (such as *varatrā*) are feminine only.

40. *Bhrātṛ*, *amitra*, *chātra*, *putra*, *mantra*, and *vṛtra* are masculine when expressing friendship. 41. *Patra*, *pātra*, *patriman*, *atra*, and *channa* are also masculine. 42. Words denoting strength, flowers, battle, cities, and war are [masculine]. 43. *Padma* and *kamala* are also masculine when expressing the lotus. 44. *Āhava* and *saṃgrāma* are masculine. 45. *Āji* is feminine only. 46. The class of fruits [is feminine]. 13. The class of trees is feminine only. 48. *Vija*, *jagat*, *sakṛt*, *kṛṣat*, *pṛṣat*, *śakṛt*, *yakṛt*, and *uśīta*. 49. *Navanīta* and *taṃ*.

The neuter forms are: *ṛta* (truth), *amṛta* (nectar), *nimitta* (cause), *vitta* (wealth), *pitta* (bile), *netra* (eye), *rajata* (silver), *vṛtta* (conduct), *pakva* (cooked), *śrāddha* (funeral rite), *kuliśa* (thunderbolt), *deva-pīṭha* (divine seat), *kuṇḍa* (pit), *adhi-sakthi* (the thigh region), *akṣi* (eye), *asthi* (bone), *āspada* (abode), *ākāśa* (sky), *kaṇva* (a sage), and *vīṇā* (lute). (50–51) The word *daiva* (divine) is used in the masculine as well. (52) The following words are neuter: *dhānya* (grain), *asra* (blood), *preṅkha* (swing), *paṇya* (merchandise), *varṇya* (to be praised), *dhiṣṇya* (dwelling), *havya* (offering to gods), *kavya* (offering to ancestors), *kāvya* (poetry), *satya* (truth), *apatya* (progeny), *mūlya* (price), *śikyaka* (sling), *kukhya* (belly), *madya* (liquor), *harmya* (palace), *tūrya* (musical instrument), and *sainya* (army). Also neuter: *dvandva* (pair), *barha* (peacock feather), *duḥkha* (suffering), *baḍiśa* (fishhook), *piccha* (tail-feather), *īśa* (lord), *kuṭumbaka* (family), *kavaca* (armor), *vara* (excellent), and *vṛndāraka* (excellent person).

54. [The following words are used in the masculine: 1. *akṣa* when meaning a sense organ; 2. *strī* and *pumān*; 3. *goman*, *yaṣṭi*, *muṣṭi*, *pāṭali*, *vasti*, *śālmali*, *truṭi*, *masi*, and *marīci*; 4. *matsya*, *sīdhu*, *karkandhu*, *sindhu*, *kaṇḍu*, and *reṇu*; 5. words ending in *-u* that denote qualities (*guṇavacana*), provided they are not neuter; 6. patronymic secondary suffixes (*apatyārtha-taddhita*). [The following words are used in the masculine and neuter: 1. *pumān* and *napuṃsaka*; 2. *ghṛta*, *bhūta*, *musta*, *kṣvelita*, *airāvata*, *pusta*, *busta*, and *lohita*; 3. *śṛṅga*, *ghoṣa*, *udyama*, *śalya*, and *dṛḍha*.

4. *vana*, *kuñja*, *kutha*, *kūrca*, *mastu*, *varṣā*, *arbhaka*, *ardharca*, and *puccha* [are neuter]. 5. Words ending in *kaba*, *anya*, and *aupāduka* [are neuter]. 6. *daṇḍa*, *maṇḍa*, *khaṇḍa*, *śava*, *saindhava*, *pārśva*, *kāśa*, *aṅkura*, *ākāśa*, *kuśa*, and *kuliśa* [are neuter]. 7. *deha*, *paṭṭa*, *paṭaha*, *aṣṭāpada*, *arbuda*, and *kakuda* [are also neuter]. 1. The remaining [words] are [determined by their] gender. 2. Indeclinables (*avyaya*), the word *kati*, and the pronouns *yuṣmad* and *asmad* [are indeclinable]. 3. Numerals ending in *ṣ* or *n* [are feminine]. 4. A heavy syllable (*guru*) and a protracted vowel (*pluta*) [are also indeclinable]. 5. The *kṛtya* suffixes [form indeclinables]. 6. The suffix *ṭ* is used in the sense of instrument (*karaṇa*) and locus (*adhikaraṇa*). 7. The group beginning with *sarva* are called pronouns (*sarvanāman*).
Thus ends the *Liṅgānuśāsana* composed by the venerable sage Pāṇini. (3) Place for obtaining the book: Khemarāja Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa, "Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara" Press, Mumbai.
